note: Crédit Mutuel de Maine-Anjou et Basse-Normandie's fee information document for the Eurocompte Confort (1 January 2026): its international deferred-debit card, a CB Mastercard or CB Visa whose month's spending the bank takes from the account at once, costs 44.40 euros a year. Crédit Mutuel's regional federations each set their own prices; this is one federation's. On 2026-10-30 the range was widened to the large national banks that publish one price list for all of France: Société Générale, BNP Paribas and LCL (Crédit Agricole's retail bank with one national list; the Crédit Agricole regional banks each set their own prices, like Crédit Mutuel's federations). La Banque Postale was tried and its site answered 403 Access Denied (Akamai), so it isn't written. Société Générale's conditions and charges for private customers in force on 1 October 2026: the CB Visa (50 euros a year), CB Visa Premier (146) and CB Visa Infinite (345) as international deferred-debit cards; BNP Paribas's conditions and charges of 1 January 2026: the Visa Classic (49.50), Visa Premier (144) and Visa Infinite (347) deferred-debit cards; LCL's tariff guide of 1 January 2026: the Visa Cléo (52.20), Visa Premier (146.40), Mastercard Platinum+ (234) and Visa Infinite (360) deferred-debit cards. Each is a card whose month's spending the bank takes from the account in one sum, so nothing is carried (rate in full). A payment outside the euro zone or in another currency costs a share plus a fixed sum: Société Générale 2.7% plus 1 euro over 10 euros (the Infinite 2% plus 1), BNP Paribas 2.90% plus 0.90 (the Infinite 2% plus 0.60), LCL 3.05% plus 1.26 (the Infinite and Platinum+ 2.38% plus 1.26); the share is written as the foreign fee, the fixed part not modelled. Each bank's revolving-credit card (Société Générale's CB Visa Alterna, 20 euros a year; LCL's Visa Crédit Renouvelable, 20 euros a year) prices its credit as 'nous consulter' in the price list, and Société Générale's Alterna page loads its rate table by script, so no rate was found and those cards aren't written; BNP Paribas stopped selling its Provisio revolving credit on 19 October 2026. The immediate-debit versions of the same cards are debit cards and aren't written; discounts for a second card, for those 18 to 24 and in packaged accounts aren't written.
